title: Fit
description:
`hpr fit`, as JSON: a design's simulation fitted to its flight's log by least squares, each
parameter with its 90% interval, each thing read from the log with where it came from.

clock_offset_s.description: The log's clock at the simulation's zero, s.

converged.description: Whether the fit ended where no step lowered its misfit further.

fitted_apogee_m.description:
The apogee of the flight at the fitted parameters, m above the pad; null if it reaches
none.

fitted_apogee_time_s.description: When the flight at the fitted parameters reaches its apogee, s from its liftoff.

fitted_max_mach.description: The top Mach number of the flight at the fitted parameters.

flown_in.description:
The conditions the fit's flights flew in, but for the wind, which the fit moves: the
launch day's where any are given, else as designed.

height_offset_m.description: What the log's pad reads above the simulation's, m.

height_read_as.description: What the log's height stands for, and so how each simulated flight's is read.

issues.description:
The known issues the flight at the fitted parameters meets: where HPR Sim's drag or
stability is known to read wrong on this flight, the fit's numbers take that error in.

kind.description: What kind of result this is: a model fitted to a measurement.

logger.description: The logger, as the log names it.

misfit_share.description: That residual as a share of the spread of the heights read.

notes.description: What to bear in mind in reading them, as the text form's notes say.

parameters.description:
Each parameter, in the fit's order: the drag scale, the impulse scale, the burn time's
scale, the wind toward the east and the north, and the structure's mass scale.

readings.description: What the fit read from the log, each with its source and provenance.

rms_m.description:
The heights' residual's RMS, m: the log's height less the fitted flight's, over the bins
read.

site.description: The launch site flown from, and where its place came from.

stated_apogee_m.description: The apogee of the flight as stated, before the fit, m above the pad.

tool.title: Tool
tool.description:
The program that wrote a document or a file: the title block every `--json` document, every
file `hpr` writes and `hpr --version` carry (ADR-164; the product system's `data.md`: "Every
export carries the designation and version of the tool that made it").

designation.description: Its designation in the FusionSpace product system: `FS-ACHERNAR · SW · TOOL 001`.

trust.description: The trust note the text form ends with.

CompareConditions.description: As designed, or on the launch day.

oneOf.description: The 1976 standard atmosphere and no wind, at the site.

The launch day's air and wind: from Open-Meteo's archive, a weather profile, or values
entered.

CompareFlownIn.description: The conditions a comparison's simulation flew in.

conditions.description: As designed, or on the launch day.

detail.description:
Where the air and wind came from, in words: the weather source, its time, place and
credit, or the values entered.

CompareSite.description: The launch site `hpr compare` flies from.

elevation_m.description: Height above sea level, m, as given.

from.description: Where the latitude and longitude came from.

FitApogee.description: The apogee a fit's window ends at.

bound_m.description: The bound the height's error stays within, m.

height_m.description: Its height above the pad, m.

provenance.description: Whether it was measured or derived.

source.description: The track it was read from.

time_bound_s.description: The bound the time's error stays within, s.

time_s.description: Its time, s on the log's clock.

FitCaveat.description:
The caveat on a fitted parameter's interval that fails its test on the synthetic flights and
is recorded as failing.

below.description: The synthetic flights whose truth lay below the interval, as recorded.

meant.description: How many a 90% interval is meant to leave below it.

message.description: The caveat in sentences, with which way the interval errs.

FitLiftoff.description: The liftoff a fit's window starts by.

bound_s.description: The bound its error stays within, s.

provenance.description: Whether it was measured or derived.

source.description: The track it was read from.

time_s.description: Its time, s on the log's clock.

FitNoInterval.description: Why a fitted parameter states no 90% interval.

oneOf.description: The fit isn't asked for it: the burn time's scale.
A log of height alone can't tell the wind.

FitParameter.description: One parameter as `hpr fit` found it.

caveat.description: The caveat its interval carries; null for an interval that passes its test.

interval_90.description: Its least-squares 90% interval; null where none is stated (`no_interval` says why).

no_interval.description: Why it states no interval; null where it states one.

standard_error.description: Its standard error, from the fit's own residuals.

stated_mean.description: The middle of what the fit was told of it before the log.

stated_sd.description: The standard deviation of what the fit was told of it.

value.description: The fit's value: a factor, or for the wind a speed in m/s.

oneOf.description: The factor on the rocket's zero-lift drag.
The factor on the motor's total impulse.
The factor on the motor's burn time: moved by the fit, not asked of it.
The constant wind's speed toward the east, m/s.
The constant wind's speed toward the north, m/s.
The factor on the structure's mass: the rocket without its motors.

FitReadings.description: What `hpr fit` read from the log.

apogee.description: The apogee the window ends at.

horizontal_track.description:
The horizontal track read, east and north of the pad from the log's latitude and
longitude; null for a log of height alone.

liftoff.description:
The liftoff the fit's window starts a second before; null for a log that starts in
flight, whose first sample stands for it.

FitTrack.description: A track of the log a fit read.

bins.description: Its quarter-second bins that hold a sample, liftoff to apogee.

bins_read.description:
The bins the fit read: a barometer's at or past Mach 0.8 on the fitted flight are left
out.

provenance.description: Whether its values were measured or derived.

HeightReadAs.description: What a log's height stands for.

oneOf.description: A barometer's reading: the standard atmosphere's altitude of the pressure, less the pad's.
A height climbed: a GNSS receiver's, or the accelerometer's integral.

IssueKind.description: Which numbers a known issue bears on.

oneOf.description: The drag: the apogee, the top speed, the drift, the flutter margin.
The stability margin and the center of pressure.

The flight's path, through something other than the drag or the margin (a moment, the
damping, the wind): the apogee and the drift.

Kind.description: What kind of result a command printed: the kind every figure in it is.

oneOf.description: From a model of the flight, not measured.
Measured: an altimeter's log, or a weather balloon's sounding.
A weather model's forecast.
A reanalysis: a weather model's fit to past observations, such as ERA5.
Copied from a data file, such as a motor's curve file, or computed from it.
A measurement set against a model: a log against a simulation of it.

A model fitted to a measurement: a simulation's inputs moved until it passes through a
log.

Peak.description: A metric's extreme and when it came.

after_apogee.description:
Whether it came after apogee, in the fall. With no recovery device opened, a peak in the
fall is not a prediction: the fall rests on small-angle aerodynamics far outside their
range.

height_above_ground_m.description: The height above the launch site then, m.

value.description: The value, in the unit the field's name gives.

ReadingInterval.description:
A reading's 90% interval: on the synthetic flights, the truth lay below `low` about 5% of the
time and above `high` about 5% (`hpr_flightdata::readings::interval`).

high.description: Its upper end, in the reading's unit.

low.description: Its lower end, in the reading's unit.

ReadingProvenance.description: Whether a reading was measured on the track, derived from it, or clipped by it.

oneOf.description: A time or height read off the filtered track.
Worked out from the track, such as a speed from its slope.
Measured, but at the sensor's range, so the true value may lie beyond it.
A provenance this build of `hpr` doesn't name.

ReadingSource.description: The height track a reading came from.

oneOf.description: The logger's own barometric altitude, the record's primary track.
A pressure channel, turned into a height by the 1976 standard atmosphere.
A barometric altitude kept in a channel, above the pad or above sea level.
A GNSS receiver's altitude: no reading is taken from it.
The accelerometer along the rocket's axis.
A source this build of `hpr` doesn't name.

SimIssue.description: A known error in HPR Sim's drag, stability or flight path that the flight meets.

issue.description:
The issue's number on GitHub: 18, 67, 68, 70, 72, 73 or 222 for drag; 179 or 354 for a
separated part's drag, also of kind drag; 64, 87, 120, 121, 172, 325, 326, 1198 or 1290
for stability; 8, 106, 213 or 219 for the flight's path, whose signs depend on the case.

message.description: What the issue means for this flight, with which way its numbers lean.

parts.description:
The ids of the parts whose shape meets the issue's condition; empty for base drag (68)
and friction (18), which every rocket has, for 121, 172, 1198 and 1290, for a separated
part's (179, 354), and for the wind's (8) and the center of gravity's (219). For 213 the
single pod sets, for 106 the body parts the supersonic join covers.

SiteFrom.description: Where a comparison's site came from.

oneOf.description: `--latitude` or `--longitude` gave it.
The median of the log's last GNSS fixes before liftoff.
The log's first GNSS fix: it holds none before liftoff.
Neither: no site was given and the log holds no GNSS fix, so 0° N, 0° E.
